references.text: Lot hesitates, but the angels take him and his family by the hand and lead them out of the city, warning them to flee without looking back
Lot's wife looks back toward Sodom and becomes a pillar of salt, illustrating the consequences of disobeying God's warnings
Jesus refers to Lot and the destruction of Sodom as an example of the importance of being prepared for God's judgment
Peter uses the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah as an example of God's judgment on ungodliness, but also how the righteous are saved
Moses warns the people to separate themselves from the wicked so they will not be swept away by their sins—a parallel to the angels' warning to Lot
An exhortation to come out of Babylon so as not to share in her sins and plagues—thematically parallel to fleeing Sodom before judgment
A parallel about an angelic warning to flee to save one's family from impending death.
The psalm formulates the theological principle that the story of Lot illustrates concretely.
